description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
Random init again; run only to print example signatures and I/O pairs from the task object.
Default shape: 3 layers with LN and MLP; only block 0 acts. One-hot token + one-hot position; W_q maps position to source address. LN calibrated to identity, MLP zeroed.
E03 with the two idle blocks removed: one layer does all the work.
E04 without the MLP: the zeroed MLP did nothing, so the block is attention only.
E05 without LayerNorm: it was calibrated to identity, so remove it. Attention plus embeddings only.
E06 with the residual removed from attention, so the output is the copied token alone and W_o needs no amplification (gain 1).
E07 with soft attention (beta=1) to find how sharp the pointer must be.
Soft attention beta=1.5: just above ln(4), testing the theory that the 4 separators in context outvote the target at beta=1.
Soft attention beta=2 (weight 7.4 vs 1): enough to beat separators and repeated letters?

Factored address: word(3) + letter slot(4) + phase(1), W_q swaps words 0 and 2 and flips phase. Separators keep their word code; expected to mis-read, since the answer's first separator mirrors to the '=' slot.
E11 with no word code on separators: a separator query matches every prompt separator, and they all hold '_'. W_q reads as: mirror the word, keep the slot, look in the prompt.
E12 with tokens as 5-bit +/- codes instead of one-hot; the head decodes by matching codes. d_model 13.
E12 with tokens as 28 points on a 2-D circle; the head picks the nearest angle. d_model 10.
Ring tokens plus ring addresses: keys on one 2-D circle, queries on another. d_model 6.
One 2-D address field: prompt positions store r(s) on a half ring, answer positions store -r(source), and W_q=-I turns that into a query. d_model 4.
E16 with W_q/W_k/W_v replaced by fixed field selection and the head tied to the token table. Params: token table, address table, beta.
E17 with each token as one number (its index); the head picks the nearest token value.
E18 with each address as one number and attention scored by negative squared distance: pos_emb is literally a table of read addresses. d_model 2.
E19 at beta=3, below the predicted limit of about 4.7 where leak from neighbouring slots shifts the averaged scalar token by half a step.
E19 at beta=5, just above the predicted limit of about 4.7.
E19 at beta=4, bisecting the failed beta=3 and working beta=5.
E19 at beta=20 with position 22 dropped from the address table, since the last character is never fed back.
Keys are position+1 by construction, so the 22-row address table shrinks to 11 read addresses for the answer positions.
E24 with the token id itself as the value, so no token table. Learnable-style state is just the 11 read addresses and beta.
Read address is linear in fixed position features: read = 9 - 4*word + letter - 4*is_sep. The 11-entry table becomes 4 coefficients.
Treat '=' as a separator by folding its value onto '_'. Then read = 9 + i - 8*word: walk forward, jump back 8 at each word boundary. 3 coefficients plus beta.
E27 at beta=5, the lowest value that passed on random prompts, checked on the worst-case a/z stress test.
E27 at beta=4.5, bisecting between beta=4 (failed in the scalar family) and beta=5 (passes).
E27 with softmax replaced by argmax, so no leakage and no beta. Only the 3 query coefficients remain, at the cost of a non-standard attention rule.
Unmodified default architecture (d_model 64, 4 heads, 3 layers, d_ff 256). Balanced ring codes make LayerNorm a constant rescale; head 0 of block 0 is the pointer and the rest is zero.
E31 at gain=5: the residual input token can tilt the read by up to 11.5 degrees, past the 6.4-degree half-step, so failures are expected.
E31 at gain=10: maximum tilt 5.7 degrees, just inside the 6.4-degree half-step, so it should pass with a thin margin. Stress test now includes the full alphabet.
E31 at beta=100: adjacent keys on the half ring differ by only 0.04, so the score gap is 4 and neighbours leak about 2 percent each.
E31 at beta=30: score gap to adjacent keys only 1.2, so neighbours and even distant keys leak heavily. Looking for where the vector average finally fails.
Every stock component kept (LayerNorm, MLP, residual, W_o) at the smallest size that fits the 8 active dims: d_model 8, 1 head, 1 layer, d_ff 1.
Stock blocks with the readable word/slot/phase address: W_q is mirror-word, keep-slot, flip-phase. Ring tokens, d_model 14, 1 head, 1 layer, d_ff 1.
E37 with centred one-hot tokens, so each output dim is a letter. d_model 38, gain 10.
E38 at gain=2: with one-hot tokens the read only has to outvote the single residual input token, so gain just above 1 should do.
E38 at beta=3, with a single-field mismatch costing only 3 score units, to measure how soft the readable circuit can be.
